chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: Anna Mae on music in the family
summary: She recalls the washboards, tin tubs and an organ, and little J. C. marching in a school concert.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: how do you feel about your brother?
Well, how would you like ... when you look back over his early beginnings and so forth ...
Well, could I go back a little bit?
Well, I don't knowx where the music came from but it seemed like it's been in the family as long
as I can remember. My parents bought an organ. Before then my sisters and brothers, they used to use washboards to make music.
Who was this and when was this?

That was before J. C. was born. And they used to use washboards and juice harps and then one time my older sister gave a ... and when they were practicing, they didn't have any instrument, they used tin tubs to bang on to make music. And they used to go around at night and serenade and sing. And when my parents got old enough, I mean when they was able, they bought an organ and ... bought a piano after that. ... music in the family and J. C., when he was a little boy, he was too young to go to school and one time my sister, she was a teacher so she gave a concert. And the children were marching around, you know, singing, playing and he was too young to be in it so he would just march and went right on up with the children. So we we just went right on up from that until the time he was old enough to go to school. And ... because I was away when he was going to high school but the family always seemed to be ... just loved music. The whole family for some reason. I don't know ... to be a doctor. I have a
grandson. He's supposed to go to England. Did Jim tell you?

: Yes.
: He's supposed to go to England in May.
A grandson, 15 years old.
: Richard's son has gone to Africa a couple of times, right?
